questions.learningObjective: Explain why a sealed can may burst when heated
questions.stem: A ticket asks why a sealed aerosol can may burst if heated; explain using gas laws.

answer.exemplar: Heating raises gas temperature in a fixed volume, increasing pressure via Gay-Lussac's law until the container fails. The pressure rise is the hazard, not volume change.

questions.explanation: Temperature rise at constant volume raises pressure. Once pressure exceeds container strength, it bursts.
questions.hint: Fixed volume plus rising temperature raises pressure.
